concepts.def: GDP per capita, HDI (UNDP), Gini, multidimensional poverty index, Inequality-adjusted HDI.
Rostow (1960): traditional, preconditions, take-off, drive to maturity, mass consumption.
Domar (1947) growth = saving ratio / capital-output ratio; underpinned Big Push aid policy.
Sen (1999) Development as Freedom: development means expanding freedoms, not just income.
Natural resource boom raises currency, harming non-resource exports; Netherlands gas in 1960s gave the name.
Yunus and Grameen Bank (1976): small loans to the poor without collateral; Nobel Peace Prize 2006.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Economic Principles and Issues — a core area of A-Level Economics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Economic Principles and Issues brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Economic Principles and Issues.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
